sufficient_sets.text: Manatees are three of the four living species in the order Sirenia. The fourth is the Eastern Hemisphere's dugong. A preexisting member of the order known as Steller's sea cow was hunted to extinction in the eighteenth century. The Sirenia are thought to have evolved from four-legged land mammals more than 60 million years ago, with the closest living relatives being the Proboscidea (elephants) and Hyracoidea (hyraxes).
